summary: Retest of undo-split fix confirms the HIGH bug from iteration_13 is closed. Full backend pytest suite = 98/98 passing (97 prior + 1 new TestPartialChainUndo). The exact repro (SP 30 ct → marking 30 → laser 30 → shape 30 → POST /packets/{laser}/undo-split) is now REFUSED with 400 'Packet is out with a karigar or its weight has already been cut into another packet'; the register still shows only the shape packet at 30 ct and the stone stays balanced. Partial-chain (A 30 → B 12 → C 5): undo of B returns exactly min(carried, weight) = 12 back to the source, C keeps its 5, total on the floor stays 30 and balance holds. All prior invariants also verified: normal leaf undo works and revives a source whose status was 'consumed'; undo refused for packets never split, packets with process entries, packets currently issued, and staff users (403). Availability pool rule regression (pool = un-packeted rough + ALL in-stock packets minus issued) still passes. UI smoke on preview URL confirms balance-bar, kapan-tab-*, sp-kapan-link-*, sp-stone-link-* render fine; no console errors.
critical_code_review_comments: undo_packet_split now correctly gates on packet.status=='in_stock' (line 1026) — blocks undo of any packet already cut into a downstream split (status='consumed') or issued to a karigar. Message is user-friendly and covers both cases.

give_back = r2(min(carried_weight, current weight)) (line 1036) is the right formula: for a partially consumed intermediate it returns only what actually still sits in the packet, so material already cut out stays with the downstream packet and total on the floor is invariant.

Suggest a follow-up (non-blocking): create_process_packets still never mutates the source packet's carried_weight when consuming from stock. Now that undo is gated on status this is safe, but if a future feature ever un-consumes a source, carried_weight will still be stale — worth normalising eventually.
seed_data_creation: All test kapans/stones are created and deleted in the same test (finally blocks). No leftover TEST_ data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Fix for chained-split undo double-count is deployed and locked in by test_undo_split_edge.py::TestChainedSplitUndoMiddle (asserts 400 refusal + balance holds) and TestPartialChainUndo (asserts mass balance holds after undoing a partially-consumed intermediate). Full pytest = 98/98 in ~31s. Next agent should keep these tests; extend the module if new undo semantics appear.
rca of the issue: Original bug: server.py::undo_packet_split blindly added packet.carried_weight to source regardless of whether the packet had been fully consumed by a downstream split. Fix (verified in place at server.py:1026-1038): (1) require packet.status == 'in_stock' (rejects consumed/issued packets with clear message); (2) give_back = min(carried_weight, current weight) — for partially-consumed intermediates only the weight that actually still sits in the packet flows back, so mass balance is preserved by construction.
